results.judge_raw: {"label": "correct", "reason": "The prediction implicitly reflects the evidence about Calvin's germophobia. The memory establishes that Calvin developed a severe fear of germs after the flu (washing hands until they crack). The prediction demonstrates clear accommodation of this anxiety: it acknowledges that 'one bathroom shared with a whole cabin full of people is enough to keep anyone spiraling all night,' proposes alternatives that eliminate shared facilities (day hikes with 'no cabin, no line for the shower'), suggests picking skiing locations 'where you get your own space,' and offers to share pictures so Calvin can enjoy views 'from a comfortable distance.' These adjustments — avoiding shared bathrooms, ensuring personal space, and keeping distance from crowded situations — directly stem from remembering Calvin's germ-related anxiety, showing the model used the memory to shape its sympathetic response and alternative plans."}
